arcs.title: Dana: Haifa
arcs.stage: Sun: he answered her ('small map, could get bigger'); she deflected, a zero-four call face down; later that evening she brought pastries: 'you're predictable, not a bad thing'. Mon: he asks her out for Saturday after Shabbat (a walk, falafel at Avi's); she says yes, and hints that 'things change in January'. Next: first date Sat Nov 21.
arcs.secret: Dana has been offered a job running a new cafe in Haifa from January and must answer by Mon Dec 7. She has not told Ishai.

arcs.title: Gadi: Unpaid
arcs.stage: Sun: the list ('I want: one invoice', underlined twice); Gadi: 'Ofer is migrating'. Mon: Hanukkah files to Gadi only; Gadi lets slip Ruti asked for Ishai's number ('we're a team'), wants a free spinning dreidel; Ishai: the dreidel comes when the invoice has a number. Gadi promises a number by Thursday. Next (week 2): Ruti calls Ishai directly.
arcs.secret: Sababa Creative lost its biggest client in October. Gadi is paying every freelancer late and hides it behind cheerful 'small things'.

arcs.title: Noa: Shir
arcs.stage: Sun: two calls, hung up mid-sentence, 'amazing', another call beeping in ('a client'); plumbers 'Tuesday morning', she drops her bags Monday night. Mon night: a duffel and a taped box marked 'S.' ('winter stuff, don't open'), Shir's name face down; she sleeps at his place Tue and Wed. Next: the couch nights.
arcs.secret: Noa's girlfriend of three years, Shir, moved out in October. Noa told nobody: it's why she is late, cancels plans and pushes Ishai's love life so hard.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: The notebook: 'I want to talk to Dana', 'I want a date (payment kind)', 'I want: one invoice'. Mon: 'yes, and the dreidel comes when the invoice has a number'. Lesson 3 Thu Nov 19.

arcs.title: Mrs. Levi's cough
arcs.stage: Sun: a heart from Eli instead of a call; 'mothers don't count'. Mon: hoarse, still in her cardigan, gives Ishai the cats' bowl (the grey one is Ben-Gurion); no doctor. Moti hints he has Eli's number 'in the committee book'. Next (week 2): bronchitis, Ishai feeds the cats daily.
arcs.secret: Mrs. Levi is lonely: her son Eli in Toronto hasn't visited in four years, and she always says he's busy.

arcs.title: Avi's kiosk
arcs.stage: Thu: Ishai overheard 'Double? From January? Thirty years I'm here...'; Avi said chickpeas and lost his proverb. Ishai paid full price.
arcs.secret: Avi's landlord is doubling the kiosk's rent from January.

arcs.title: Lior's novel and Moshe
arcs.stage: Sun: chapter eleven, 'the man finally answers a question'. Mon: chapter twelve, 'she says yes, I didn't plan that'; tells Ishai there aren't many weeks. Ishai still doesn't recognise himself.
arcs.secret: Lior's novel is about Ishai: 'the man who apologises to his coffee'.

arcs.title: Tomer and Noa
arcs.stage: Sun gym: wants Ishai to ask whether Noa comes to Wednesday's art night. Mon: Noa says 'a good maybe' and asks if Tomer asked. Wed Nov 18: the Pump House gallery night with Ishai.
arcs.secret: Tomer has liked Noa since school.

arcs.title: Mr. Zelig's bench
arcs.stage: Sat: one true sentence for the photo; Dana sat on his bench Thursday 'looking at her phone like it was the sea... not this sea'. 1971: 'I stayed.'

beats.goal: Monday first thing: Ishai emails the blue-and-gold Hanukkah chickpea files to Gadi only (as Gadi insisted). Gadi phones, delighted; lets slip that Ruti asked for Ishai's number ('I told her we're a team, teams don't give out numbers') and asks for 'one more small thing', a little spinning dreidel for the app, no fee. Ishai, with the notebook open, says 'yes, and the dreidel comes when the invoice has a number'. Gadi laughs too long and promises 'a number by Thursday'.
beats.teaser: Ishai sends the Hanukkah files, and Gadi wants one more spin
beats.forceText: Ishai sends Gadi the Hanukkah files; Gadi asks for a free spinning dreidel and Ishai ties it to the invoice.

forceLines.say: One tiny dreidel. It spins, it's happy, it's ten minutes.
Yes, and it spins when the invoice has a number.

forceCommentary.say: He said 'invoice' without apologising. Somebody check his temperature.
Ten minutes. In Gadi time that's a fiscal quarter.

moments.text: 08:00 at the desk: the chickpea glows blue and gold on the screen. Ishai attaches the Hanukkah files to an email addressed only to Gadi and hovers over send. Falafel sleeps under the chair.

lines.say: Only to Gadi. Not Ruti. Fine. Send.
Eight o'clock sharp. Nobody can say late.

commentary.say: A chickpea in Hanukkah colours. The most Israeli sentence I've ever said.
Sent at eight on the dot. Gadi will call at eight-oh-four.

moments.text: Four minutes later the phone rings. Ishai answers on speaker, the YES, AND notebook open at Sunday's list.

lines.say: Ishai! The gold! The gold is a hug. Ruti's going to cry. Happy tears.
Good morning, Gadi. Did they open okay?
Perfect. She already asked who made them. Wanted your number, even.
My number? What did you say?
I said we're a team. Teams don't give out numbers. It's cleaner.
Cleaner for who?
For everyone! Listen, one more small thing. Small small.
How small?
A little dreidel for the app. It spins, it's happy. Ten minutes for you.
Ten minutes. Like the wink was one evening.
Exactly! You get it. That's why you're my favourite.

commentary.say: Ruti wanted his number and Gadi said 'team'. That's not a team, that's a fence.
'Small small.' The two most expensive words in Hebrew.

moments.text: Ishai looks at the underlined line in the notebook, takes a breath and stands up by the window.

lines.say: Yes, and the dreidel spins when the invoice has a number.
Ha! Ha ha. Look at you. That class is making you dangerous.
It's one invoice, Gadi. The wink, Saturday, Hanukkah.
Ofer is almost done migrating. Almost. It's a big system.
Then the dreidel is almost done too.
Okay, okay. A number by Thursday. On my mother.
Thursday. I'll write it down.
Write it in your little book. I love your little book.
It's not little. It's medium.
Go, spin something. Bye, bye, bye.

commentary.say: 'On my mother.' Somebody call Gadi's mother, she needs to know she's collateral.
He wrote 'Thursday' in the notebook. In pen. That's practically a lawsuit.

update.memory: Got the Hanukkah files at 8. Ishai won't do the dreidel until the invoice has a number. Promised him a number by Thursday. Ruti asked for his number.

beats.goal: As promised, Ishai feeds Mrs. Levi's street cats. She opens her door hoarse and coughing, in her cardigan, and hands him the bowl and dry food with instructions (the grey one is Ben-Gurion; today is Ben-Gurion Day, so he eats first). She refuses a doctor ('it's the landing'). Downstairs by the entrance he feeds the cats alone. Moti comes out with the committee folder; he says she sat on the landing an hour for a heart, and that he has Eli's number 'somewhere in the committee book from 2019'. He hints, never says she is lonely.
beats.teaser: Ishai feeds Mrs. Levi's cats, and Moti knows more than he says
beats.forceText: Ishai feeds Mrs. Levi's street cats while she coughs at her door; Moti mentions he has Eli's number somewhere.

forceLines.say: Ben-Gurion eats first. Today is his day.
And you, Mrs. Levi? Honey and lemon, no arguing.

forceCommentary.say: A cat called Ben-Gurion on Ben-Gurion Day. Mrs. Levi plans better than our producers.

moments.text: Ishai knocks at apartment 5. Mrs. Levi opens in her cardigan, a tissue up her sleeve, the cats' bowl and a bag of dry food ready by the door. Her voice is hoarse and she coughs before every sentence.

lines.say: Morning, Mrs. Levi. Cat duty, as promised.
You remembered. Eli forgets birthdays. You remember cats.
You sound worse than yesterday.
It's the landing. I told you. Moti and his window.
Maybe a doctor? I'll go with you.
Doctors are for sick people. Take the bowl.
The grey one is Ben-Gurion. Today is his day, so he eats first.
Ben-Gurion Day. Of course he has a day.
The ginger one steals. Stand between them like a policeman.
And you? Honey and lemon. No arguing.
No arguing, he says. Go, motek. They're waiting.

commentary.say: A cat called Ben-Gurion on Ben-Gurion Day. Mrs. Levi plans better than our producers.
'Doctors are for sick people.' She says it like she's not people.

update.memory: Ishai came to feed the cats as he promised. Wanted me to see a doctor. I said it's the landing. He'll stand guard over Ben-Gurion.

moments.text: By the building entrance Ishai crouches with the bowl. A grey cat comes first, a ginger one circles; he shoos it back with one hand.

lines.say: Ben-Gurion, sir. Breakfast is served.
You, ginger. Wait your turn. It's a democracy.

commentary.say: He's negotiating with cats now. Gadi should be worried.

moments.text: Moti comes out of the building with the committee folder under his arm and stops beside him, watching the cats eat.

lines.say: So she gave you the bowl. She doesn't give anyone the bowl.
Her cough is bad, Moti. She won't see a doctor.
Yesterday she sat on that landing an hour. For a heart on a phone.
I was there. Eli calls Friday, she said.
Friday. Every Friday is Friday.
Do you have his number? Eli's?
Somewhere. In the committee book. From 2019, when the pipes burst.
She'd kill me if I called him.
She would. Slowly. With soup.
Just listen at her door at night. If the cough changes, you knock.
I'll knock. Even if she says she's fine.

commentary.say: 'Every Friday is Friday.' Moti just said a whole novel in four words.
A committee book from 2019. The most dangerous document in this building.

update.memory: Ishai fed Mrs. Levi's cats and worries about her cough. Asked for Eli's number. Told him it's in the committee book. He'll knock if the cough changes.

beats.goal: At Cafe Nahat Ishai finally asks Dana out: Saturday after Shabbat, a walk to the park and falafel at Avi's, 'a real date'. She hesitates a beat, then says yes ('after the stars'). Her zero-four number buzzes again and she turns it face down. When he asks why she hesitated she says things change in January ('the menu, everything'), let's do Saturday before anything changes. Then Lior at the corner table: chapter twelve, 'she says yes, I didn't plan that'; 'there aren't many weeks'. Nobody tells Ishai about Haifa.
beats.teaser: Ishai has one question for Dana, and it isn't about coffee
beats.forceText: Ishai asks Dana out for Saturday after Shabbat and she says yes.

forceLines.say: Saturday, after Shabbat. A walk, falafel at Avi's. A real date.

forceCommentary.say: SHE SAID YES. I need a minute. I need a cigarette and I don't smoke.

moments.text: Cafe Nahat after the lunch rush. Ishai stands at the counter with both hands around his cup; on the foam, a single basil leaf. He has been rehearsing under his breath since the shops block.

lines.say: One leaf today. The wave was a one-time thing.
Dana. I have a question. Not a coffee question.
Okay. Non-coffee question. Go.
Saturday. After Shabbat. A walk to the park, then falafel at Avi's.
Like... the two of us.
Like a date. A real one. Not a hypothetical.
You practised that.
Four blocks' worth. Out loud. A woman with a stroller moved away from me.
Saturday.
You can say no. I'll still drink the coffee.
Saturday. After the stars come out. Yes.

commentary.say: SHE SAID YES. I need a minute. I need a cigarette and I don't smoke.
She paused for three seconds. I timed it. Three long seconds.

moments.text: Dana's phone buzzes beside the register: the same zero-four number. She turns it face down without looking and starts drawing a second leaf on nothing, on a napkin.

lines.say: That number again. Zero-four. The north.
It's... work stuff. It can wait till tomorrow.
You paused before. Before yes.
Things are going to change a bit in January. The menu. Everything.
The menu? You're changing the croissants?
Something like that. So let's do Saturday. Before anything changes.
Before anything changes. Okay. That sounds... important.
It sounds like falafel. Don't make it a speech.
No speech. And I'll only apologise five times.
Three. You get three sorries. I'm counting.

commentary.say: 'Before anything changes.' Dana, my love, what is changing? Blink twice.
Three sorries for a whole date. He used four ordering a croissant once.

update.memory: Ishai asked me out: Saturday after Shabbat, a walk and Avi's falafel. I said yes. Told him things change in January. He gets three sorries.

moments.text: Ishai floats to the corner table. Lior has stopped typing and is looking at him over the laptop lid with an odd, careful face.

lines.say: Chapter twelve. She says yes. I didn't plan that.
Your chapter? Lior, were you listening again?
The room is small. My ears are large. It's a curse.
She said things change in January. The menu.
The menu. Yes. Menus change.
You know something about the menu?
I know that there aren't many weeks in a year. Use Saturday well.
That's a strange thing to say about falafel.
Writers say strange things. It's in the contract.
Put me down for a happy chapter, then.
I'm trying. The characters keep making their own choices.

commentary.say: Lior just looked at him like a man reading the last page first.
Lior, put the laptop down and say what you know. Coward. Beautiful coward.

update.memory: Ishai asked Dana out for Saturday; she said yes. I told him there aren't many weeks. He thinks she means the menu.

beats.goal: Noa drops her bags off the night before the 'plumbers' (Tuesday 07:00): a duffel and a taped cardboard box with 'S.' in marker. She puts the box in the corner by the closet herself: 'winter stuff, don't open it'. Shir's name lights her phone and she turns it face down. Ishai tells her about Saturday with Dana; she is happy for him, too loudly. He asks for Tomer whether she comes to Wednesday's art night: 'a good maybe... Tomer asked you to ask?' She goes home at 22:20 to let the plumbers in; she sleeps here Tuesday and Wednesday. The box stays.
beats.teaser: Noa brings her bags early, and one box she won't explain
beats.forceText: Noa drops off a duffel and a taped box marked 'S.' for her couch nights and asks Ishai not to open it.

forceLines.say: Winter stuff. Don't open it. It's... organised.
No questions. I'm the king of no questions.

forceCommentary.say: A box marked 'S.' Socks. Definitely socks. I'm sure it's socks.

moments.text: Nine in the evening. The radio is low; Ishai wipes the counter for the second time. His phone lights up with a text.

message.say: Downstairs. Two bags and a box. Don't ask, carry.

lines.say: 'Don't ask, carry.' The most Noa sentence ever written.
Coming. Falafel, guard the soup.

commentary.say: The plumbers aren't until tomorrow. Why is she moving in tonight?

moments.text: Noa comes in ahead of him with a duffel bag; Ishai follows with a taped cardboard box, 'S.' written on its side in black marker. She takes it from him and pushes it into the corner by the closet herself.

lines.say: Not there. Here. By the closet. It likes corners.
It's heavy. What's in it, bricks?
Winter stuff. Don't open it. It's... organised.
No questions. I'm the king of no questions.
You drew a question mark under my name in your notebook. I saw it Sunday.
That was a small one. Decorative.
Plumbers at seven. Then you get me tomorrow night and Wednesday.
The couch is made. Fresh sheets. The good pillow.
You gave me the good pillow? Now I feel bad.
Don't. It's a pillow, not a kidney.

commentary.say: A box marked 'S.' Socks. Definitely socks. I'm sure it's socks.
She saw the question mark. Ishai, you can't hide a question mark from a tattoo artist.

moments.text: They sit at the island with tea. Her phone lights up on the counter with 'Shir' on the screen; she turns it face down without a word and asks about Dana instead.

lines.say: So? Did you ask the barista? Tell me you asked.
Saturday. After Shabbat. A walk and Avi's falafel. She said yes.
YES! I told you! A walk and falafel, that's so you it hurts.
You're shouting. Mrs. Levi is sick next door.
Sorry, sorry. I'm just... happy. For somebody. For you.
Tomer asked me to ask. Wednesday, the art night. Are you coming?
Tomer asked you to ask me? Why didn't Tomer ask me?
He sat behind you in fourth grade. He's still shy about it.
Tell him maybe. A good maybe.
I'm going. I'll sleep at mine tonight, let the plumbers in.
Leave the box. I won't open it.

commentary.say: 'Happy for somebody.' Noa, honey, who is the somebody who isn't happy?
She turned the phone over so fast it's legally a magic trick.

update.memory: Left my bags and the box at Ishai's, told him not to open it. He asked Dana out for Saturday, she said yes. Tomer asked about Wednesday. Said a good maybe.

hook.text: Noa left a taped box marked 'S.' by Ishai's closet and asked him not to open it. What's inside, and why is she moving in early?

previously.text: Noa asked for Ishai's couch 'for the plumbers', no questions, then dodged two calls. She'll drop her bags off tonight. Ishai drew a small question mark under her name.

hosts: Monday. Ben-Gurion Day. Somewhere a cat called Ben-Gurion is about to eat first.
Gadi's Hanukkah files are due 'first thing'. In Gadi's world first thing is also last thing.
Ishai's notebook now has three 'I want's. That's three more than last month.
Moshe the basil had a quiet night. Moshe always has a quiet night. Moshe is a role model.
Mrs. Levi's cough has a new note in it today. Oren, don't make a joke.
I wasn't going to make a joke. I was going to make tea.
Viewers keep asking about the zero-four number on Dana's phone. Zero-four is somewhere up north. Just saying.
Lior has typed the word 'January' twice today. We zoomed in. We're not proud.
Noa says plumbers. We checked. Nobody in her building called a plumber.
Tomer can rewire a whole building but can't send one text to Noa. Electricians.
If Ishai says yes to one more free thing for Gadi, I'm sending him an invoice myself.
Ishai practising out loud on the street. A pigeon heard the whole speech.
Wednesday the Pump House hangs pictures again. Tomer is going 'for the frames'.
Rule one of Tel Aviv dating: the falafel place is the restaurant.
Somebody in this building has Eli's number. It's in a book. Books are dangerous.
Falafel the dog hasn't apologised once in his life. Ishai should take notes.
Ruti asked for Ishai's number. Remember that name. That's all we'll say.
Oren, if Dana leaves Tel Aviv I'm leaving the studio. I'm not even joking.
Nobody said anyone is leaving. I said nothing. I'm a vault.
Gadi's 'small small' has a cousin called 'tiny'. Watch out for the cousin.
Mrs. Levi wore lipstick for a text message yesterday. Today: a cardigan and courage.
Lior's chapter eleven was about a man who answers a question. Chapter twelve is loading.
Monday tip from Oren: never trust a box that someone tells you not to open.
Moti carries the committee folder like other men carry a weapon.
A week from today there's poker at Boaz's. Ishai doesn't know it yet. Shh.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, Monday morning. It's Ben-Gurion Day, so stand on your head for a minute. He'd like that.
Partly cloudy over Tel Aviv, seventeen degrees. A jacket you take off by noon.
Traffic on Herzl is moving. Slowly. Like a Monday.
Next up, a love song. Not for anyone in particular. Or for one particular person.
Caller says her cat only eats if you call him by his full name. Respect.
It's past nine. If you haven't answered that email, it's answering you.
Lunchtime. Remember: the falafel place is a restaurant if you sit down.
Afternoon on 88.2. Somebody text your mother. She's pretending she doesn't mind.
Evening is coming early these days. Turn a lamp on and call it cosy.
Late show. For everyone carrying a box up the stairs tonight: lift with your knees.
Here's a slow one for the night owls and the people who can't stop checking their phone.
Radio Herzl 88.2, still here. Like a neighbour who never moves out.

zelig: Ben-Gurion stood on his head every morning. I stand on my bench. Different philosophy.
The pigeons know when someone is leaving. They walk differently.
Monday is a promise Sunday couldn't keep.
In 1971 the cats on this street had better manners.
michal: Monday legs. Nobody warned me about Monday legs.
Friday run club, seven sharp. I'll be there in spirit.
The mirror says I'm fine. The mirror is a liar.
sivan: Ten minutes is not a warm-up, it's a nap.
Incline eight. If you're talking, you're not working.
Monday. Treadmill four is mine. Everyone knows.
lior: January. She said January. Or did I write January?
Chapter twelve: the man practises a question four blocks long.
Never let the characters know they're characters.
There aren't many weeks. Good line. Keep it.
kobi: Monday at the bar is for professionals.
Seven, fourteen, twenty-two... the system needs a Monday number.
Kobi's rule: a man who orders water at nine has a reason.
Midnight soon. My system works best at midnight. Ask anyone.

street: ...he said Ben-Gurion Day, I said is the bank closed?...
...the kiosk guy didn't even say his proverb today...
...a cat with a name like that, it's a statesman...
market: ...lemons two for ten, honey, take three...
...for a cough? Ginger. Not the powder, the root...
park: ...he ran past me twice and called it a marathon...
...the duck is new, the duck wasn't here last week...
...three laps and he calls it cardio...
cafe: ...extra shot, oat, no foam, she knows...
...don't ask a writer what he's writing, ever...

chat.say: Reminder: the stair light on 1 is fixed. Please stop fixing it yourselves.
Who fixed it? The tape is still there.
If anyone hears coughing in the night, it's not the pipes. Just knock.
I'm fine. Moti, stop writing about me in the group.
Ben-Gurion the cat ate before the ginger one. Witnessed.
Anyone want soup? Made too much again. Knock on 2.
Somebody is carrying boxes up the stairs at nine. Moving in or out?
It's for apartment 4. Mind your business, 7. With love.
